subtype: Approach: loosens the rule and keeps the parts that helped [Revision]
passage: Yogesh, you look like Nikhil did at your age: phone in hand, guilt on the face. Let me tell you what I did. I once locked all my apps from nine to six, because games were eating my life. For three days I felt strong. On the fourth day my manager needed a file and my work chat was locked. I broke the lock in a panic and dropped the whole thing for a month. Then I sat down and asked: what was working? The evening games block was working. What was not? Blocking the work apps. So I made the rule smaller: games locked from six to eleven at night, work apps free at all times. It still holds two years later.

qa.q: When are games locked under the new rule?
qa.a: Games are locked from six to eleven at night.

qa.q: How did Nikhil feel on the fourth day when the manager needed the file?
qa.a: Nikhil felt panicked, and broke the lock in a hurry.

qa.q: Which turning point inside the story helped, and why?
qa.a: Asking what was working and what was not showed that the games block helped while blocking work apps hurt, so only the second part was changed.

qa.q: How might the manager have felt while waiting for the file?
qa.a: The manager might have felt impatient or worried about the delay, and puzzled that Nikhil could not open the chat.

grounding: Shows a person loosening a strict phone lock, keeping the evening games block and freeing work apps during the day.
